findings.claim: Spaces before a \verb delimiter leak verbatim content into prose and can bypass the mandatory overlap check.
findings.evidence: Static trace, not executed: verb_end() uses the character immediately after \verb or its star as the delimiter. For valid '\verb |x y|', that character is a space, so the scanner blanks only '\verb |x ' and leaves 'y|' as prose. Consequently, 'We measure the roughness of lunar \verb |x y| and martian terrain at baselines from' inserts y between the two six-word halves of the abstract at test_overlap_check.py:27-30, and shared_runs() finds no 12-word run. Similarly, '\verb |x seamless|' leaks seamless and produces a false lint finding. The pinned v33 bundle's latex.ltx:11086 defines \@sverb to skip spaces before its delimiter; :11106-11112 routes \verb through that reader. Existing extraction tests at test_tex_prose.py:102-114 cover only adjacent delimiters. Skip permitted spaces before selecting the delimiter and add extraction and consumer regressions.

resolution.reason: Reproduced: \verb |x y| took the space as delimiter and left y| in the prose, hiding the 12-word run. latex.ltx (bundle v33) lines 11086 and 11106-11112: \verb makes the space other before \@ifstar, and \@sverb skips spaces before the delimiter. verb_end now skips tabs before the star and spaces and tabs before the delimiter (\verb |x y|, \verb* |x|, \verb *x* are verbatim). Regressions in 1c888fc: extraction cases with line count, unclosed cases, dash, banned-word and question rules, and the overlap run.
